- Model consistently overestimates prices, especially in the early part of the forecast horizon (first 5–10 days).
- Forecasts tend to peak too early and overshoot, particularly after sharp upward spikes in history.
- Model underestimates prices in the final 5–10 days of the forecast, suggesting a lag in recognizing downward momentum or mean reversion.
- Forecasts show persistent bias toward higher values, especially when history includes recent high prices.
- Model fails to capture mean reversion in the latter half of the forecast, often holding prices too high when true outcomes trend lower.
- Overshoots are more common after price spikes, suggesting model lacks sufficient dampening or smoothing after volatility events.
- Model underestimates low-price periods, especially when history includes recent dips — may be underweighting downside risk or lagging in response to policy or supply shocks.
